t: #3527 Find the Most Common Response — Dedupe Then Count
o: Within each day, duplicate responses count once, so first collapse each day's list to a set; then count across days. Example 1: after dedupe, "good" appears in 3 days and wins. Ties break to the lexicographically smallest string, so select by (−count, string).
k: Dedupe per day with a set before counting — repetition within a day must not inflate frequency.
Selection key: highest count, then lexicographically smallest.

a.n: Approach 1: Hash Counter with Tie-Aware Minimum
a.i: Feed Counter.update with each day's set, then pick min by (−frequency, word).
s: For each day, insert set(day) into a global counter.
a.t: O(total responses) — hashing each string once (times its length)

w: Straightforward; the only trap is forgetting the per-day dedupe, which changes answers whenever a word repeats inside one day. Follow-up: return the top-k responses, or stream days without holding everything in memory.
